---
title: "Stocks and years in the stockpile"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 8
)
options(width = 100)
```

This article shows what has been submitted to the stockpile: which stocks,
which years they cover, and whether there are observed data, model estimates
or both. The stocks are grouped by the ICES expert group that assesses them,
which is looked up in the ICES Stock Database with the
[icesSD](https://github.com/ices-tools-prod/icesSD) package.

It is run against the live stock database each time this site is built.

```{r}
library(FLStockpile)
library(icesSD)
library(ggplot2)

options(FLStockpile.url = "https://github.com/neilcampbelll/FLstockpile/releases/download/v2026.001")
```

## Expert groups

The stock database lists the stocks that are active in a year, with the
expert group and data category of each. The latest version of each stock
assessment in the stockpile is matched to it by stock code and assessment
year.

```{r}
stocks <- stockpile_stocks()

stock_database <- lapply(unique(stocks$assessment_year), function(year) {
  sd <- getSD(year = year)
  data.frame(
    stock_code = sd$StockKeyLabel,
    assessment_year = year,
    expert_group = sd$ExpertGroup,
    data_category = sd$DataCategory,
    species = sd$SpeciesCommonName
  )
})
stock_database <- do.call(rbind, stock_database)

stocks <- merge(stocks, stock_database, all.x = TRUE)
stocks$expert_group[is.na(stocks$expert_group)] <- "not in the stock database"

# what the stockpile has for each stock assessment
stocks$contents <- ifelse(
  stocks$observed & stocks$estimated, "observed and estimated",
  ifelse(stocks$estimated, "estimated only", "observed only")
)
stocks$contents <- factor(stocks$contents, c("observed and estimated", "estimated only", "observed only"))

# a label for each stock assessment
stocks$assessment <- paste0(stocks$stock_code, " (", stocks$assessment_year, ")")

contents_colours <- c("observed and estimated" = "#1b9e77", "estimated only" = "#7570b3", "observed only" = "#d95f02")
```

The stockpile has `r nrow(stocks)` stock assessments, of
`r length(unique(stocks$stock_code))` stocks, from
`r length(unique(stocks$expert_group))` expert groups.

```{r, fig.height = 4.5, fig.alt = "Horizontal bar chart of the number of stock assessments in the stockpile for each expert group, with the bars divided into observed and estimated, estimated only and observed only."}
ggplot(stocks, aes(y = reorder(expert_group, expert_group, length), fill = contents)) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = function(limits) seq(0, limits[2], by = 2)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = contents_colours) +
  labs(x = "stock assessments in the stockpile", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

### How much of each expert group's work is in the stockpile

The stockpile holds age-based assessments, which are mostly the stocks in data
category 1. For the most recent assessment year, the number of stocks each
expert group has in the stock database, the number of those in category 1, and
the number that are in the stockpile:

```{r}
latest_year <- max(stocks$assessment_year)
active <- stock_database[stock_database$assessment_year == latest_year, ]
active$category_1 <- floor(as.numeric(active$data_category)) == 1
active$in_stockpile <- active$stock_code %in% stocks$stock_code[stocks$assessment_year == latest_year]

coverage <- aggregate(cbind(stocks = 1, category_1, in_stockpile) ~ expert_group, active, sum, na.action = na.pass)
coverage <- coverage[coverage$in_stockpile > 0, ]
coverage <- coverage[order(-coverage$in_stockpile), ]

knitr::kable(
  coverage,
  row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = c("Expert group", paste("Stocks in", latest_year), "In category 1", "In the stockpile")
)
```

## Years

The years covered by the observed data and by the model estimates of each
stock, from the ranges of the submitted objects. Where the estimates run past
the assessment year, they include a forecast.

```{r, fig.height = 11, fig.alt = "For each stock assessment, grouped by expert group, horizontal lines showing the range of years covered by the observed data and by the model estimates."}
sources <- stockpile_sources()
sources <- sources[sources$class == "FLStock", ]
sources <- merge(sources, stocks[c("stock_code", "assessment_year", "version", "expert_group", "assessment")])

ggplot(sources, aes(y = assessment, colour = type)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = min_year, xmax = max_year), linewidth = 1.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  facet_grid(expert_group ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(observed = "#d95f02", estimated = "#1b9e77")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing = unit(0.6, "lines")
  )
```

The same as a table, with the ages and what else is known about each stock:

```{r}
ranges <- stocks[order(stocks$expert_group, stocks$stock_code, stocks$assessment_year), ]
ranges$years <- paste(ranges$min_year, ranges$max_year, sep = "–")
ranges$ages <- paste(ranges$min_age, ranges$max_age, sep = "–")

knitr::kable(
  ranges[c("expert_group", "stock_code", "species", "assessment_year", "data_category", "years", "ages", "contents", "indices")],
  row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = c(
    "Expert group", "Stock", "Species", "Assessment year", "Category", "Years", "Ages", "Contents", "Survey indices"
  )
)
```

## Submissions

When each version of a stock assessment was submitted. A stock with more than
one version has been corrected since it was first submitted.

```{r, fig.height = 4.5, fig.alt = "Dates on which versions of stock assessments were submitted, by expert group, with first versions and corrections marked differently."}
versions <- stockpile_stocks(version = "all")
versions <- merge(versions, unique(stocks[c("stock_code", "assessment_year", "expert_group")]))
versions$submission <- ifelse(versions$version == 1, "first version", "correction")

ggplot(versions, aes(as.Date(submitted), reorder(expert_group, as.numeric(submitted), min), colour = submission)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.7, position = position_jitter(width = 0, height = 0.15, seed = 1)) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("first version" = "#1b9e77", "correction" = "#d95f02")) +
  labs(x = "submitted", y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The stock assessments with more than one version:

```{r}
corrected <- versions[ave(versions$version, versions$stock_code, versions$assessment_year, FUN = max) > 1, ]
corrected <- corrected[order(corrected$stock_code, corrected$version), ]
corrected$submitted <- format(corrected$submitted, "%Y-%m-%d")

knitr::kable(
  corrected[c("expert_group", "stock_code", "assessment_year", "version", "submitted", "latest")],
  row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = c("Expert group", "Stock", "Assessment year", "Version", "Submitted", "Latest")
)
```
